subject: Post-demo: migration feasibility & hyperscaler comparison — next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@finlytics.com>, Tim Porter <tim.porter@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: migration feasibility & hyperscaler comparison — next steps

Hi Sara / Tim —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed short plan to move from discovery -> an evaluation you can run with minimal lift. Notes below are high-level; I attached a simple matrix and a short OpenAI-compat sample that Marcus will seed into the test harness.

Key takeaways from the call:
- FinLytics cares most about predictable latency (95th %ile < 300ms for short queries), low token cost for high-throughput batching, and an easy migration path from your current hyperscaler endpoints (OpenAI-compatible surface).
- You currently run a mix of OCI/BigCloud-hosted models and OpenAI endpoints for inference; procurement wants clear cost delta and compatibility guarantees before proceeding.
- Security posture: SOC2 + VPC peering is required; you flagged audit log retention and KMS integration.

Proposed short evaluation (3-week cadence):
1) Baseline run (week 0): run our supplied OpenAI-compat sample on your existing endpoint(s) to capture prompt/response diffs (we'll provide prompt IDs and expected metrics).
2) Compatibility smoke tests (week 1): SDK swap demonstration (Python/Node) using our OpenAI-compatible endpoint; regression tests for the 10 highest-traffic prompts. Marcus will provide test harness scripts.
3) Performance head-to-head (week 2): 95th/99th latency, cold-start, and batching cost run comparing your hyperscaler baseline vs Redwood Dedicated (we'll supply a standardized load generator).
4) Procurement packet (week 3): cost delta sheet, SLA language draft, and a short security checklist for your auditors.

Immediate asks from you:
- Can you share a sanitized sample of the top 10 prompt patterns (redacted) by Wed EOD so Marcus can map them into the harness?
- Who on your infra side should we loop in for the VPC/KMS questions?

Attachments included:
- proposal-diff-matrix.xlsx (proposal / comparison matrix)
- openai-compat-sample-reqs.txt (sample requests + expected response markers)

Next steps: Marcus will follow-up with the harness and a short runbook. I'll set up two 30-minute checkpoints next week (compat smoke test + perf planning). If procurement wants numbers earlier, we can accelerate the cost delta draft.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0143

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: migration feasibility & hyperscaler comparison — next steps

Thanks Neha — adding the harness + minimal instructions here. Sara, I'm dropping a short test harness (zip in Drive link) with the following files:
- run_harness.py (python 3.10) - loads sample prompts and compares tokenization + response checksums
- openai_client_config.json - minimal config to point at your current OpenAI-compatible endpoint or the Redwood test endpoint
- readme.md - steps to run locally or in your CI (no elevated permissions required)

A couple of notes on the SDK swap / compatibility points to watch for:
- Header handling: some hyperscaler wrappers add an X-Request-ID header that mutates the response trace; our harness normalizes headers before diffing.
- Streaming semantics: we'll compare both chunked streaming and full-response behavior; SDKs sometimes have slight differences in newline handling which appear as false positives in diffs.
- Tokenization: we include the exact tokenizer we used in the sandbox; mismatch here explains many prompt deltas.

I'll plan to seed the harness with the prompts Neha requests; if you can send them to me directly (marcus.lin@redwood.ai) I'll map them into the 10 canonical cases.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: migration feasibility & hyperscaler comparison — next steps

Neha / Marcus —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side:
- We'll redact PII and share the top 10 prompt patterns by Tue noon. Expect examples that highlight short queries (~10–30 tokens) and a set of longer multi-turn prompts used in our decisioning flows.
- For infra, loop in Carla Mendes (carla.mendes@finlytics.com) — she'll be point for VPC/KMS and will want the audit-log retention details.
- Procurement asked if you can provide a first-pass cost delta table (ballpark) before the perf head-to-head so they can decide whether to proceed with a 3-week effort. If you can provide an estimate range (delta per 1M tokens) that would help.

Also: Tim flagged that we run a small proprietary re-ranking step that is latency-sensitive — we need to see how Redwood batching affects p95. Please include a test that mirrors our re-ranker (we can provide the code sample).

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Product | FinLytics Analytics
